text: The memory of Josiah is pleasant, like skillfully mixed incense or the taste of honey, or like music at a banquet where wine is served.
He did right and led the nation to get rid of its idols and turn back to God.
Many had rejected God's Law, but Josiah was faithful and encouraged others to obey God.
David, Hezekiah, and Josiah were good kings, but the other kings of Judah sinned terribly and rejected the Law of God Most High. So he took away their kingdom
and gave their glorious power to foreigners
who burned down Jerusalem, the city God had chosen for his temple. The city streets lay empty, just as Jeremiah had said.
He had been chosen as a prophet before his birth and was later told to speak of doom and destruction, of rising and rebuilding. But the evil kings of Judah mistreated him.
Ezekiel saw a vision of the Lord's glory above the living creatures that were his chariot.
God said that Job always did what was right.
I pray that the twelve prophets will live on in their descendants because they helped Israel stand firm during hard times by giving them hope.
What is the best way to praise Zerubbabel? He was like a valuable ring on the Lord's right hand,
as was Joshua son of Jozadak. They built a holy temple for the Lord, and it will always be famous.
We should honor Nehemiah because he rebuilt the homes in Jerusalem; he repaired the city walls and put in strong new gates.
No one like Enoch has ever been born— he was taken up from earth to heaven.
And no one like Joseph has ever been born— he kept Israel from starving and ruled his brothers; then after his death, the people of Israel watched over his bones.
Shem and Seth are also honored, but of all God's creatures, Adam was the greatest.
